content.title: Ronda Rousey vs Gina Carano card suffers blow as injury forces ex-UFC star to withdraw
content.text: Lorenz Larkin has been forced to withdraw from his appearance on the Ronda Rousey vs Gina Carano bill.Larkin was set to take on former Bellator champion Jason Jackson in a welterweight showdown on the blockbuster bill.2Larkin has been taken off of the event after suffering an injuryCredit: GettyThe bout was set to take place on May 18 but will no longer feature.That is because Larkin has suffered a knee injury in training.He released a statement on social media confirming he would no longer be able to compete and has withdrawn.It read: "I’m sorry to all the fans, but I had to pull out due to a knee injury."I’ll be rehabbing it back to 100% and will be back.”Larkin will be disappointed given it represented a big payday for MMA fighters.Rousey herself had even confirmed that all fighters stood to earn a minimum base purse of $40,000 on the night.If Paul puts on another MMA event, Larkin will no doubt again be keen to get back involved given he is a free agent.Rousey vs Carano - a historic eventThe event will see Rousey return for the first time since 2016.It will be the first MMA event to feature on streaming service Netflix, and will be more new ground for the trailblazer.2Rousey and Carano will headline a mammoth commercial eventCredit: GettyShe believes it will be a game changer once again for women's sport and MMA.Rousey said: "I think that fighting for MVP and on Netflix, it makes this fight bigger than us. "It's a game-changer for the entire industry. And I think that everything's going to be different for all of the fighters after this. "This is an experiment that Netflix is undertaking, and I think that we're going to outperform every single expectation on this card.Well, I think it's getting to a point where it's not a novelty to have women headlining events becoming commonplace. "Hopefully, it's so common that it doesn't even deserve a mention. UFC ScheduleFor all the upcoming fights and results this year, check out talkSPORT.com's UFC schedule."I think the ultimate goal is for women to have the same views and bring in the same revenue as the men and to be able to be compensated the same as them as well."At the launch press conference for the May 16 Netflix event last month, Rousey blasted the UFC for its 'poverty-level' fighter pay.And when she took to the stage in New York on Wednesday, the UFC's finances were once again under the microscope as she revealed that MVP's base pay is four times higher than MMA's premier promotion.“I think it’s really important that we raise the ceiling, but also raise the floor," said Rousey, who is co-promoting the event alongside MVP."One thing that I’m really proud of on this card is that the absolute minimum anybody will walk away with, even if they don’t have a big, long record, and even if they lose, it’s $40,000."“If you fight 3 times a year, that is much more than a living wage."That’s something the UFC cannot say... And I hope that after this event, we can continue to raise that ceiling higher and higher until it is on par with the highest-level boxers."
